about: cesr.parse cases that must be rejected, each a well-formed stream (a genus/version code, a KERI 2.0 inception framed by its version string, attachments) with exactly one thing broken. The specification states almost no parser-side rejection rule, so each assertion rests on the MUST the stream violates and carries a note saying so; that classification is pending a policy decision and will not change the case ids.

cases.title: Reject a stream that ends inside a signature
cases.description: A KERI 2.0 inception, then an attachments group holding a -K of one signature, with the last two bytes of the stream removed. The -C and -K sizes promise 22 quadlets of signature and the stream holds 21.5. The adapter protocol makes the end of the input final (a harness rule, not a specification claim), so a parser may not wait for more bytes. The specification has no sentence saying such a stream must be rejected; the assertion rests on the cited MUST, which this stream violates.

cases.title: Reject a signature group whose size ends it inside a signature
cases.description: Inside an attachments group, a -K of size 21 holds an 88-character (22-quadlet) signature: -K ends four characters before the signature does, and those four characters then sit inside -C where no element can start. The specification has no sentence saying such a stream must be rejected; the assertion rests on the cited MUST, which this stream violates.

cases.title: Reject an attachment count code whose second character selects no defined table
cases.description: After a KERI 2.0 inception, the attachment position holds the count code -0AB, whose second character is the numeral 0. The specification reserves numerals for other count code tables and genus 2.00 defines none, so the code is an error. (keripy 1.x used -0 as its big-count selector; genus 2.00 uses --.)

cases.title: Reject an indexed signature whose pad bits are not zero
cases.description: An A# indexed signature, in a -K after a KERI 2.0 inception, whose pad bits between the index and the value are not zero. The raw value bits are untouched. The specification has no sentence saying such a stream must be rejected; the assertion rests on the cited MUST, which this stream violates.

cases.title: Reject a stream that resumes with a bare primitive
cases.description: After a KERI 2.0 inception and its attachments group, the stream continues with a D key and no count code. Its first byte, 'D', has the tritet 0b010, which the stream-start table reserves for a text-domain op code ('_'); 'D' is neither an op code nor a count code, and no field map or annotation starts with it, so the stream does not resume with any of the eight permitted frames. The specification has no sentence saying such a stream must be rejected; the assertion rests on the cited MUST, which this stream violates.

cases.title: Reject a body shorter than its version string declares
cases.description: A KERI 2.0 inception with the last five bytes of the stream removed, so the body is shorter than the size its version string declares. The adapter protocol makes the end of the input final (a harness rule, not a specification claim), so a parser may not wait for more bytes. The specification has no sentence saying such a stream must be rejected; the assertion rests on the cited MUST, which this stream violates.
